Grade III (severe) Any organ failing: BP needs medicine support; reduced consciousness; poor oxygen; low urine or creatinine above 2.0 mg/dL (~177 µmol/L); INR above 1.5; platelets below 100
Grade II (moderate) Any of: WBC above 18; tender lump in right upper tummy; symptoms more than 72 hours; severe local inflammation on scan
Grade I (mild) Neither of the above Early keyhole operation
A — inflammation Fever above 38 °C and/or shaking chills; WBC below 4 or above 10; CRP 10 mg/L or more
B — bile blocked Jaundice (bilirubin 2 mg/dL ≈ 34 µmol/L or more); liver tests above 1.5 × upper limit
C — scan Widened bile duct; cause seen (stone, narrowing)
Diagnosis Definite = A + B + C; suspected = A + (B or C) → EMERGENCY: sepsis care + urgent drainage (ERCP)
Fever/shivers AND yellow skin/eyes AND right upper pain? Cholangitis — EMERGENCY: sepsis bundle, senior, urgent ERCP
Stone seen in duct on scan, OR bilirubin above 68 with duct wider than 6 mm? HIGH risk of duct stone: planned operation is usually deferred; senior; ERCP pathway
Any liver test abnormal, OR age over 55, OR duct wide? INTERMEDIATE risk: senior; MRCP (or EUS) to look for a stone
LOW risk → continue with planned operation

Risk factors include: age over 60, BMI over 30, cancer, previous clot, family history of clots, oestrogen pill or HRT, pregnancy, dehydration, reduced mobility, surgery longer than 90 minutes, acute tummy inflammation.
Bleeding risk factors: active bleeding, blood thinners, platelets below 75, very high BP.
NICE quality standard QS216 asks hospitals to use a validated risk tool. Options: SORT (Surgical Outcome Risk Tool, simple), P-POSSUM, ACS NSQIP online calculator.
